svg.title: The same theorem at two cardinalities: for arbitrary languages the completion needs the Boolean prime ideal theorem, a choice principle, while for countable languages it is weak Koenig's lemma, a compactness principle provable in ZF

g.text: "Every consistent theory has a complete consistent extension"
one statement, and the cardinality of the language decides what it costs
Unprovable in ZF. Strictly weaker than AC
(Halpern and Levy 1971). Zorn on the poset of
proper filters: a genuine limit stage, and the
union at that stage is what must be chosen.
Sharp condition: the algebra is NOT well-orderable.
A ZF theorem. Walk the enumeration, decide one
element at a time, every stage a successor.
Nothing is chosen. Measured finely in reverse
mathematics, the strength is exactly WKL₀.
So the principle the layered architecture actually needs is COMPACTNESS, not CHOICE.
Low Basis Theorem (Jockusch and Soare 1972): the completion exists, is not computable, and is LOW.
